title: Rest And Still Rise (R&B Flow)
style: contemporary r&b with hip-hop flow, 84-94 bpm, crisp programmed drums with tight hats, deep sub bass, Rhodes chord stabs, bright synth plucks, smooth sung r&b hook, call-and-response ad-libs, confident swagger, dry upfront vocal, radio-ready mix. Warm female lead sings the hook with sustained notes; the verses are rhythmic rap with clear diction over the beat. The lead SPEAKS the lines tagged Spoken in a plain natural voice over the music, RAPS the lines tagged Rap with confident metered flow, and SINGS the lines tagged Sung with long held notes. The intro and the outro are spoken; the full band keeps playing continuously under them, natural resolved ending, final chord rings out and fades. Sing the sections in the order written; the song never opens with the hook: build up through the verse first.
negative_tags: choir, reverb, echo, band dropout, acapella sections, talk-singing, monotone delivery

segments.lyrics:
[Intro (spoken): close dry voice, plain speech, no melody]
Running on empty.

[Vocalise (sung): wordless, full melodic voice, two very long held notes]
Ooh-oo-ooh, ooh-oo-ooh

[Verse 1 (rap): rhythmic rap on the beat, tight metered flow, clear diction]
Alarm at five and I'm already behind on the day,

[Pre-Chorus (sung): smooth r&b melody, rhymed]
I'm running out of ro-oom,
I'm fading in the glo-oom,

[Verse 2 (rap): rhythmic rap on the beat, tight metered flow, clear diction]
Two in the morning and the numbers just will not add,

[Pre-Hook (sung): smooth r&b melody, rhymed]
My daughter saw my fa-ace,
she saw me lose my pla-ace,

[Instrumental Break: band only, no vocals]

[Product (sung): smooth r&b melody, clear diction on the name]
She handed me a bo-ook,
The Unhurried Year, just look,

[Hook (sung): smooth r&b melody, sustained notes, clear diction]
You can rest and still ri-i-ise,
the morning in your e-eyes

[Hook (sung): smooth r&b melody, sustained notes, clear diction]
You can rest and still ri-i-ise,
the morning in your e-eyes

[Outro (spoken): calm close voice, plain speech, no melody]
The Unhurried Year by Dana Wells. Tap the link.
